skills.evidence: Strong grasp of data structures and algorithms, and the ability to reason about time and space complexity under pressure
Hands-on programming ability — you can turn a problem statement into working, efficient code quickly
Experience or coursework in object-oriented design and common design patterns, with an eye for extensible, maintainable architecture
Comfort reasoning about system design at scale — able to sketch how a large distributed system like a URL shortener or a file storage service might be built
Working knowledge of operating systems fundamentals (processes, threads, virtual memory)
Working knowledge of core networking concepts (TCP/UDP, HTTP, how a web request actually travels)
Clear written and verbal communication — able to explain a technical tradeoff to engineers and non-engineers alike, and to disagree productively with a teammate
Solid software engineering fundamentals: testing strategy, code review habits, awareness of technical debt, and basic CI/CD concepts
